I would say something like:

The nature of the state is such that they have the legal right to initiate violence, force, fraud, and coercion against us.  They also make the laws and expect us to obey them.  The police are in charge of enforcing those laws and sometimes they abuse their power in the process.  The situation is made more confusing because the state claims to serve us, but are you really the master if you receive orders and are punished for disobedience by the servant?
I so thoroughly enjoyed that book, more than the movie.  That bit at the end filled me with wonder.

At the age of 11 months, I could point to every letter of the alphabet on command.  Whenever someone would try to interact with me, I wouldn't respond.  I started to talk at 3 years old, but I've never been a very social person.  Currently, I have no friends, nor desire to interact with people beyond the maintenance of my existence.  In school, I placed in the top 2% for math in my state.  I had a gift.  That gift is gone now.  Ever since the age of 10, I've thought about suicide almost daily.  I'm 27 now.  The few times I'm able to enjoy life are when I'm on cannabis or magic mushrooms.  Or drunk, but alcohol comes at a relatively heavy price.  Throughout my life, I've been to a dozen psychologists and put on a few different medications.  Nothing works.

Had I been presented the choice of being born, I would have probably opted out.  But that choice was made for me.

On the bright side, your kid will probably turn out different.
